# SpriteAnimationHandle

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Animation` · struct

```csharp
public readonly struct SpriteAnimationHandle
```

One play of an animation on a [`SpriteAnimationPlayer`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md), returned by [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Play`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#play), for setting actions on its frames and for when it finishes.

## Remarks

A play has one action slot per frame ([`When`](#when)) and one for when it finishes ([`Then`](#then)); setting a slot again replaces it. Another [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Play`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#play) of a different animation, a restart, or [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Stop`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#stop) interrupts the play and empties its slots without running them, so a chain built on it stops by itself and nothing needs to be unsubscribed. A handle from an interrupted play does nothing.

Actions run synchronously inside [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Update`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#update).

## Properties

### IsNewPlay

```csharp
public bool IsNewPlay { get; }
```

Whether [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Play`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#play) started this play, rather than finding it already going. A game that calls `Play` every frame can set its actions only then, instead of allocating a closure each frame:

```csharp
var play = player.Play(isMoving ? run : idle);
if (play.IsNewPlay) { play.Then(() => ...); }
```

## Methods

### Then

```csharp
public void Then(Action action)
```

Sets the action to run when this play of a [`PlaybackMode.Once`](PlaybackMode.md#once) animation finishes, replacing any set before. Not run if the play is interrupted first, or if it has already finished, and never for a looping animation.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `action` | The action to run. |

The action runs synchronously inside [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Update`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#update). An animation played from it starts with the time left over from that update, so the hand-off lands on the exact frame.

Because the slot holds one action, calling this again for the same play (for example from a state machine that calls `Play(...).Then(...)` every frame) replaces it rather than adding another.

### When

```csharp
public SpriteAnimationHandle When(int frameIndex, Action action)
```

Sets the action to run whenever this play enters a frame, such as a footstep or a hit, replacing any set before for that frame.

| Parameter | |
|---|---|
| `frameIndex` | The frame's index in the animation's frames. |
| `action` | The action to run. |

**Returns:** This handle, for setting more actions.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** `frameIndex` isn't a frame of the animation.

The action runs every time playback enters the frame: on each loop of a looping animation, and twice per pass for a middle frame of a ping-pong. It runs even when an update skips over the frame on screen, so a hit frame isn't lost to a slow frame; the frames an update enters run in order, at most one pass's worth per update.

The play's first frame is entered when it starts, so its action runs on the next [`SpriteAnimationPlayer.Update`](SpriteAnimationPlayer.md#update). The last frame of a [`PlaybackMode.Once`](PlaybackMode.md#once) animation runs its action before [`Then`](#then).
